newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco drafts laws on new parliament.
newsitem.headline: Morocco drafts laws on new parliament.

text.p: Morocco's government on Wednesday unveiled draft laws for a two-house parliament in the country's drive to widen political representation in a multi-party monarchial democracy

Interior Minister Driss Basri outlined the 86-article draft for the 303-seat lower house, known as the Chamber of Representatives, and the 55-article draft on the 255-seat upper house, named Chamber of Counsellors, on Wednesday at a cabinet meeting, the official news agency MAP said.
The two houses will form the Moroccan parliament according to constitutional reforms endorsed by a referendum last September.

"The two drafts aim to implement the terms of the constitution which renovated and enriched the Moroccan parliamentary system with a bicameral representation supported by Morocco's specific characteristics," said MAP quoting Basri as addressing the cabinet meeting.

It quoted Basri as saying the government and opposition parties had reached an accord on the two drafts except for details on replacing colours by symbols on voting papers and the actual method of balloting. These, it said, were under thorough study, the results of which would be submited to King Hassan. The king has urged the government and opposition parties to work together to resolve possible divergencies through compromise and understanding.
According to the constitution, the lower house will be directly elected and the upper house indirectly.
Morocco had set a tentative date for a general election to be held in September, but local newspapers on Wednesday said this could be deferred until November or even later.
